name: AEO
tagline: 10 endpoints for auditing how AI engines fetch, parse, and cite your content, plus llm-ready chunking.
persona: For AI-discovery teams, agencies, and content engineers measuring AEO posture across pages and competitors.

endpoints.summary: Orchestrator over 8-9 component AEO probes for a single URL.
Diff a domain's AEO posture against named competitors.
Likelihood that AI engines cite this page.
Coverage of JSON-LD schema types vs intent.
Simulate fetch from GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot.
Audit an existing llms.txt for completeness and link rot.
Report robots.txt posture for 14 named AI crawlers.
Detect list, table, definition, and FAQ snippet formats.
Fetch and token-chunk a page for downstream AEO scoring or RAG ingest.

recipe.title: Audit then iterate
steps: Run /v1/aeo/page-audit against the target URL to get an aggregate score plus component breakdowns.
For any sub-score below threshold, call the corresponding component endpoint (e.g. /v1/aeo/schema-coverage, /v1/aeo/heading-hierarchy-score) to see the underlying findings.
Apply fixes, then re-run /v1/aeo/llm-fetch-simulator with the GPTBot and PerplexityBot user-agents to confirm the rendered page reaches the bot intact.
Track over time by storing the page-audit JSON keyed by URL + run timestamp.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/aeo/page-audit",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"url": "https://example.com/pricing"},
    timeout=60.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: Does page-audit count as one call or many?
faq.a: One call, 3 credits. The orchestrator runs ~9 probes server-side but you only pay once and only refund once on error.

faq.q: Which AI bots does llm-fetch-simulator emulate?
faq.a: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, and Amazonbot, with each user-agent string verbatim from their published docs.

faq.q: Can I run AEO checks on a page behind login?
faq.a: No. AEO endpoints fetch as the named bot would, which means anonymously. Gate-removed preview URLs are the workaround.

name: SEO
tagline: 13 endpoints for technical SEO: meta, schema, redirects, broken links, mixed content, plus crawlability.
persona: For SEO consultants and in-house technical SEO leads.

endpoints.summary: Title, description, canonical, og, and twitter card audit.
Six readability formulas (Flesch, FK grade, Gunning, ARI, SMOG, Coleman-Liau).
Walk 301/302/308 chains and tag each hop.
Crawl and report 4xx/5xx links on a page.
Keyword surfacing with TF and density bands.
Follow and tag a redirect chain from a starting URL.
Fetch with auto-escalation through the render cascade.

recipe.title: Page-level technical audit
steps: Pull the sitemap with /v1/intel/sitemap to get a URL inventory plus lastmod.
For each URL, call /v1/seo/meta-audit and /v1/seo/schema-validate in parallel to score on-page tags.
Run /v1/seo/broken-links-audit and /v1/seo/redirect-chain-map on high-traffic pages to catch dangling links and redirect loops.
Roll the per-URL JSON into a single client-facing report and store deltas between runs.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/seo/meta-audit",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"url": "https://example.com/blog/seo-checklist"},
    timeout=30.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: Does broken-links-audit follow off-site links?
faq.a: Yes, but only HEAD-checks them. It will not crawl beyond the seed page.

faq.q: What schema.org version does schema-validate target?
faq.a: Latest schema.org core plus pending. We do not enforce Google's rich-results subset — use the report's `google_eligibility` flag.

faq.q: Why does meta-audit sometimes report missing og tags on pages that render them client-side?
faq.a: Server-rendered HTML is what counts for crawlers. If your og tags are injected by JS, escalate to /v1/scrape/smart so we get the rendered DOM, then re-run meta-audit on that HTML.

name: DNS
tagline: 6 endpoints for DNS lookups, propagation checks, certificate-transparency search, and subdomain enumeration.
persona: For DevOps doing migrations, security researchers, and domain investigators.

endpoints.summary: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, and CNAME per record type.
Resolver-diverse summary of a domain's DNS posture.
Propagation status across geographically distributed resolvers.
Subdomain discovery via certificate transparency logs.

recipe.title: Migration cutover check
steps: Before the cutover, snapshot the current state with /v1/dns/intelligence to capture all record types in one payload.
Push the DNS change at the registrar.
Poll /v1/intel/dns-propagation every 30 seconds until target resolvers in your priority regions return the new value.
After propagation, call /v1/intel/cert-transparency-history to confirm the new certificate was logged and trusted CAs picked it up.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/dns/intelligence",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"domain": "example.com"},
    timeout=30.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: Which resolvers does dns-propagation hit?
faq.a: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Google 8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4, Quad9 9.9.9.9, OpenDNS, plus regional resolvers in EU, APAC, and SA. Result includes per-resolver answers so you can detect splits.

faq.q: How fresh is cert-transparency-history?
faq.a: Bound by crt.sh's own ingest lag — typically minutes to a couple of hours after CA log submission. We do not cache.

faq.q: Does subdomain-enumerate brute-force or only use CT logs?
faq.a: CT logs only. That misses wildcard certs but avoids generating any traffic at the target. If you need active enumeration, run it yourself and feed candidates into /v1/dns/lookup.

name: Email
tagline: 4 endpoints for email deliverability: verification, SPF / DKIM / DMARC posture, contact extraction, format parsing.
persona: For outbound sales, ESP integrators, fraud and onboarding teams.

endpoints.summary: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC posture for a domain.
Pull emails, phones, and socials from a page.
Parse an address into local-part, domain, plus-tag, and display-name.

recipe.title: List hygiene before send
steps: Parse each address with /v1/parse/email to normalize and strip plus-tags before deduplication.
Call /v1/verify/email on the deduped list to drop syntactic failures, MX-less domains, and disposable providers.
For surviving addresses, call /v1/intel/email-auth on the domain to flag any sending domains with no DMARC alignment — those are higher bounce risk.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/verify/email",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"email": "jane@example.com"},
    timeout=15.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: Do you do SMTP RCPT-TO probing?
faq.a: No. We stop at syntactic checks, MX resolution, and disposable-domain matching. SMTP probes get IPs blacklisted and producers false-negatives on greylisting servers.

faq.q: Will you flag @ollagraph.com or @qcrawl.com as nonexistent?
faq.a: No — both are catch-all domains in our knowledge base. They always validate as deliverable at the MX level.

faq.q: Why does email-auth sometimes return DMARC `policy=none`?
faq.a: That is the published policy at the domain. We report what the DNS says; we do not infer intent.

name: Domain Intelligence
tagline: 13 endpoints for WHOIS, ASN, GeoIP, SSL, IP reputation, blacklist, plus caller-request inspection and HTTP-version probing.
persona: For security teams, sign-up enrichment pipelines, fraud detection, compliance, SRE audits.

endpoints.summary: TLS certificate, chain, issuer, and validity.
ASN, announcing organisation, and prefix coverage.
Country, city, and coordinates from an IP.
Tor, cloud, datacenter, and CDN flagging.
What the internet sees about the caller: IP, geoIP, ASN, reputation, parsed User-Agent, curated header echo. One call replaces five.
Detect HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 (TLS ALPN), and HTTP/3 (Alt-Svc) support, plus TLS version, cipher, and HSTS posture.
HTML summary, meta, and canonical hints.

recipe.title: Sign-up enrichment + risk score
steps: On signup, take the email domain and call /v1/enrich/company to attach firmographics.
Take the request IP and call /v1/intel/ip-reputation plus /v1/intel/geoip — flag Tor, datacenter IPs, and country mismatches against the billing address.
If the domain is unknown, run /v1/intel/whois and /v1/intel/cert-transparency-history to check age and CA history. A week-old domain with one DV cert is a fraud signal.
Compose into a single risk score and decide allow / step-up / block.

r = httpx.post(

faq.q: What sources feed ip-reputation?
faq.a: Tor exit-node lists (live), public datacenter/cloud ASN ranges (refreshed daily), and CDN-owned prefixes. We do not subscribe to commercial threat feeds.

faq.q: How big can a geoip/bulk batch be?
faq.a: Up to 1000 IPs per call. We charge one credit per call, not per IP.

faq.q: Does enrich/company give me employee counts and funding?
faq.a: Domain, industry, country, and size band only. We do not resell funding-round data.

name: Scraping
tagline: 13 endpoints for single, batch, async, smart, and llm-ready scraping, plus extraction, crawl, and captcha solve.
persona: For AI agents, data engineers, and RAG pipelines fetching the live web.

endpoints.summary: Fetch and token-chunk for RAG ingest.
Schema-driven extract via JSON schema input.
Recursive crawl with depth and budget caps.
Automatic captcha solve flow for sites behind a challenge.

recipe.title: RAG ingest of a site section
steps: Call /v1/crawl with the seed URL, max_depth=2, and a same-host filter to discover candidate pages.
For each discovered URL, call /v1/scrape/llm-ready to fetch and token-chunk in one step.
Embed the chunks and write to your vector store. We do not persist any scraped content — your store is the only record.
On pages that come back bot-blocked, retry through /v1/scrape/smart, which auto-escalates to the render backend and then to residential proxy if needed.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/scrape/smart",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"url": "https://example.com/article", "render_js": True},
    timeout=60.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: What's the difference between /scrape and /scrape/smart?
faq.a: /scrape is a direct fetch. /scrape/smart auto-escalates: direct first, then internal render backend, then Spider.cloud ISP proxy on 401/403/429. Same response shape from all tiers.

faq.q: How do I get residential proxy?
faq.a: Pass `use_residential_proxy: true` on /scrape or /scrape/smart. It adds a +3 credit surcharge on top of the base 1 credit per call.

faq.q: Do you store the HTML I scrape?
faq.a: No. We never persist scraped content — only the URL, status, and credit-event metadata for your usage log.

name: Conversion
tagline: 7 endpoints converting PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, HTML, and image OCR to clean markdown.
persona: For RAG ingest, knowledge-base pipelines, and document-processing SaaS.

recipe.title: Mixed-format knowledge-base ingest
steps: Inspect the file's MIME type and route to the corresponding /v1/convert/* endpoint.
For scanned PDFs where pdf-to-markdown returns empty or very low text density, fall back to /v1/convert/ocr page by page.
Post-process the returned markdown into chunks of your preferred size, embed, and write to your store.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/convert/pdf-to-markdown",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"url": "https://example.com/whitepaper.pdf"},
    timeout=120.0,
)

faq.q: Can I send the file body inline or only a URL?
faq.a: Both. Pass `url` for us to fetch, or `file_b64` for an inline base64 body. Inline is capped at 25 MB; URL fetches at 100 MB.

faq.q: Does pdf-to-markdown preserve tables?
faq.a: Yes, as markdown table syntax when the layout is recoverable. Complex multi-column layouts with merged cells degrade to plain text rows.

faq.q: What OCR engine backs /convert/ocr?
faq.a: Tesseract 5 in our standard tier. Layout-aware OCR (Docling) is in pilot on a separate worker — contact us for access.

name: Site Audit
tagline: 10 endpoints composing AEO + SEO + Intelligence into a full domain health check.
persona: For agencies running monthly client audits combining uptime, security, SEO, and AEO.

endpoints.summary: Orchestrator AEO audit for the page.

recipe.title: Monthly client audit
steps: Start with /v1/intel/uptime and /v1/intel/ssl on the apex to score availability and certificate health.
Pull /v1/intel/sitemap and /v1/intel/robots to confirm crawlability, then sample 5-10 top pages from the sitemap.
For each sampled page run /v1/aeo/page-audit, /v1/seo/schema-validate, /v1/seo/broken-links-audit, /v1/seo/redirect-chain-map, and /v1/seo/mixed-content.
Aggregate into a single client-facing report, score against last month's run, and call out regressions.

samples.python:
import httpx, os

r = httpx.post(
    "https://api.ollagraph.com/v1/intel/uptime",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OLLAGRAPH_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"url": "https://example.com"},
    timeout=30.0,
)
print(r.json())

faq.q: How many credits does a full site-audit run cost?
faq.a: Per page sampled: 3 (page-audit) + 8 x 1 = 11 credits, plus 2 credits for the domain-level uptime and SSL probes. A 10-page audit lands around 112 credits.

faq.q: Can I run site-audit endpoints in parallel?
faq.a: Yes. All 10 are independent and idempotent. Your rate limit applies as the only constraint.

faq.q: Do you store a history for diffing month-over-month?
faq.a: No — we do not persist response bodies. Save the JSON yourself, keyed by domain + run date, and diff client-side.
